title: Unpack circuit boards to an ESD mat: ground each gripper, keep the foam cup away
instruction: Move both green circuit boards from their silver shielding boxes onto the grey ESD mat. A gripper may touch a board only after closing on the gold ground stud, and must close on it again after it touches the white foam cup. Before taking a board out, move the cup onto the yellow square at the back right: it must stay at least 30 cm from every board that is out of its box. Boards may rest only in their boxes or on the mat; set them down flat and apart, and do not knock the cup over.
context: Electronics assemblers (O*NET 51-2028) build the boards that go into servers and AI accelerators under an electrostatic discharge (ESD) control programme such as ANSI/ESD S20.20: whoever handles a board is grounded first, boards rest only on static-dissipative surfaces or in shielding packaging, and insulators the job does not need, such as a foam cup, are kept at least 30 cm (12 in) from any exposed board. A discharge too small to feel can damage parts with no visible sign, so the order of the steps matters as much as where the boards end up. Here the grippers are not permanently grounded: each must be discharged on the ground stud before it touches a board, and touching the foam cup can charge it again. Each shielding box is out of the other arm's reach, so each arm grounds itself and unpacks its own board; both reach the mat. The discipline is scored at every step, not just the end.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Eight things are on the table. (1) ESD mat: a grey static-dissipative rubber mat, 220 x 200 mm and 3 mm thick (220 mm along x), fixed to the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0. (2) Ground stud: a gold-plated brass post standing for the bench's common ground point, 20 mm across and 60 mm tall, fixed upright at x 14.0 cm, y 0, 4 cm behind the mat. (3) and (4) Two shielding boxes: silver metallised open-top boxes, four walls 6 mm thick and 25 mm tall round a 140 x 140 mm floor, fixed to the table, centred at x 41.0 cm, y +32.0 cm (the left box, in front of the left arm) and x 41.0 cm, y -32.0 cm (the right box); in simulation the table top is their floor. (5) and (6) Two circuit boards: each a green circuit board in its conductive plastic carrier frame, modelled as one loose box 120 x 60 x 20 mm, 80 g (the frame is mostly open), lying flat and centred in one shielding box, long side along x; both 120 x 60 mm faces look alike. (7) Foam cup: a loose white lidded expanded-polystyrene cup with a little cold coffee left in it, modelled as a solid upright cylinder 50 mm across and 70 mm tall, 30 g, standing on the mat at x 30.0 cm, y -5.0 cm, where the right board will go. (8) Parking square: a yellow plastic marker plate, 80 x 80 mm and 2 mm thick, fixed in the back right corner of the table, centred at x 8.0 cm, y -60.0 cm, outside the work area; a cup standing on it is 33 cm from a board lifted out of the right box and 48 cm from the mat. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Every control step the scorer reads both boards and the cup and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, the point between its finger tips, and its opening (0 closed, 1 open: fingers 94 mm apart). It does not see a gripper's heading, so the fingers are taken to fill a round zone about its axis: a flat-ended cylinder from the finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper, its radius reaching a finger's outer corner (half the finger gap plus the 8 mm finger thickness, and half the fingers' 27 mm width across; 57 mm fully open). Outlines (seen from above) and distances to objects use world-aligned bounding boxes. A gripper becomes grounded when it closes on the stud: its tool point within 15 mm horizontally of the stud's axis, its finger-tip point at least 5 mm below the stud's top, and its opening 0.40 or less (fingers at most 37.6 mm apart). It loses its grounding when its finger zone comes within 5 mm of the cup. A gripper touches a board when its finger zone comes within 5 mm of it. A board is out of its box unless its centre is over a box's 140 x 140 mm floor and its lowest point is below the box's 25 mm rim. Rules: (1) a gripper touches a board while not grounded; (2) a board corner is under 1 mm above the table top, or below it, at a point over neither the mat nor a box's floor (within 2 mm of its walls), or the board rests on the yellow square (lowest point within 3 mm of its top, outlines overlapping); (3) a board tilts over 30 degrees (either 120 x 60 mm face may be down); (4) the cup tilts over 30 degrees from upright, or leaves the table (its lowest point over 10 mm below the table top). The cup rule is kept if, at every step, the cup's outline was at least 30 cm from that of every board out of its box. 'On the mat within d': a board tilted under 5 degrees, its lowest point within 3 mm of the mat's top, its outline past the mat's edge by at most d. A gripper has 'let go' when its opening is 0.9 or more (fingers at least 84.5 mm apart) or its finger zone is more than 10 mm from both boards. Score 0 if any of rules 1 to 4 is broken at any moment, whatever follows. Otherwise: 1.0 if both boards are on the mat within 0 mm, their outlines at least 20 mm apart, both grippers have let go and the cup rule was kept; 0.75 if both are on the mat within 15 mm and the cup rule was kept; 0.5 if one board is on the mat within 15 mm and the cup rule was kept, or both are but it was not; 0.25 if neither is, the cup rule was kept, both grippers are grounded and the cup's outline is at least 30 cm from both boards'; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both boards still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, touches, groundings and cup contacts are not recorded and 'let go' is taken as met. In a real trial a continuity buzzer on the stud shows each grounding; the rest is judged from top and side video with a 30 cm scale bar.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The mat, stud, boxes and square are fixed; the boards and the cup are uniform shapes of the stated sizes and masses (a real cup is hollow and holds liquid). Charge, discharge and grounding are not simulated: the rules are scored from where the fingers, boards and cup are and from each gripper's opening. A gripper's heading is not read, so its fingers count as a round zone as wide as their outer corners.
reset_notes: Put each board back flat and centred in its shielding box, long side along x, and stand the cup back upright on the mat at x 30.0 cm, y -5.0 cm. Nothing is consumed.
